testbench.name: comparator-kickback
testbench.description: Charge kicked back into the comparator's input nodes by one decision, over PVT: the peak disturbance at the 1 kohm source impedance README.md's kickback row is stated at, and the residual differential/common-mode displacement of a floating high-impedance input -- including its signal-dependent part, the only component that cannot be absorbed as an offset.
testbench.claim: HARNESS PLUMBING ONLY while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder. Once a real design/ netlist is bound, this bench substantiates README.md#target-specification's Kickback row (<= 5 mV disturbance into a 1 kohm source impedance at the input nodes, single decision edge; <= 2 mV stretch).

kick_1k_peak_mv.description: THE ROW-FACING NUMBER AND THIS BENCH'S CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR: peak disturbance of an input node, relative to its own driving source, during one decision, with a 1 kohm series source impedance and 100 fF of node capacitance -- the exact condition README.md's kickback row states. The bounds here are a sanity envelope only (a true zero would mean the probe is not connected; half a rail would mean the input pair is being driven, not disturbed); the SPEC bound is deliberately not encoded while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder. The per-axis floors make `--sabotage-corners` fail: the peak is set by the input devices' C_gd/C_gs and by the front end's bandwidth, and both move with process and temperature. Floors calibrated from the full 45-point mos grid measured in this experiment's first committed record (named in this experiment's README.md), with ~45 % margin below the observed weakest slice, following the sibling repo's calibrate-from-a-cited-clean-tree-record convention. Observed weakest slices there: process 34.76 %, temperature 3.34 %, supply 15.25 %. Temperature is genuinely the weak axis here and its floor is set accordingly -- it is still more than an order of magnitude above the ~0 % a runner stuck on one temperature would produce. This is the one bench whose anchor DOES carry a supply floor, because the kicked charge scales with the rail the regeneration nodes swing between.

kick_sigdep_nv.description: THE COMPONENT THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS: the difference between the residual differential kickback at a 100 mV residue and at a 1 mV residue, on a floating high-impedance input. A residue-INDEPENDENT disturbance is indistinguishable from comparator offset and is removed by the same means; only the residue-DEPENDENT part is an irreducible error. Recorded in nV because the near-zero-referenced probes resolve it three decades below what a raw node difference can (see kick_resid_raw_uv). The ceiling is a sanity envelope, not a budget.

kick_resid_small_nv.description: Residual differential displacement left on a floating 1 pF input node after one decision, at a 1 mV residue -- i.e. the part of the kickback that never recovers because there is no low-impedance path to restore it (RC = 1 ms against a ~30 ns cycle). Bounded loosely on purpose: a residue-independent residual is an offset, and the offset budget already has a row of its own. The bound exists so 'constant' cannot quietly become 'large enough to eat that budget by itself'.

kick_cm_nv.description: Common-mode displacement of the two floating input nodes over one decision. Rejected by a differential comparator to first order, so it is not a linearity error -- but a large common-mode kick would move the operating point the offset and noise records were taken about, which is a different way of being wrong. The +/-20 mV band is a sanity envelope on that.

kick_resid_raw_uv.description: THE SAME RESIDUAL, MEASURED THE NAIVE WAY, and it is in the record to make a methodology point rather than a design one. It differences two ~1.2 V node levels, so ngspice's ~6-significant-digit `meas` result precision quantizes it at ~1 uV -- which for a well-isolated input stage is coarser than the quantity itself, and every value comes back as an exact integer number of microvolts. kick_resid_small_nv measures the identical physical quantity through a near-zero-referenced probe and resolves it ~1000x finer. Keeping both means a reader can see the resolution floor rather than take this bench's word for it.

q_resid_small_ac.description: The residual differential kick expressed as CHARGE on the 1 pF floating node, in attocoulombs, so a reader whose input capacitance differs from this bench's can rescale it. Kickback is a charge injection; quoting it only as a voltage hides its dependence on the capacitance it was measured against.

dout_1k_end.description: The 1 kohm-driven instance must still DECIDE CORRECTLY while its own kickback is disturbing its input. A comparator whose kickback pushed the input past the decision point would fail here, and that failure would be invisible in the displacement numbers alone.

dout_float_small_end.description: the same for the floating instance at a 1 mV residue -- the harder case, because nothing restores the injected charge.

dout_float_big_end.description: the same at a 100 mV residue.
